Prevention: Follow recommended orchard management practices (regular pruning, optimum manuring and fertilization, weed management etc.)
Bird-scaring tactics in orchard to avoid avian seed dispersal.
The small fruits of the weed are berries which are ingested by birds and the undigested seeds are deposited with their excrement on the branches of other trees.
The weed starts to germinate on the branches.
Monitoring: Loranthus is a woody bushy plant which grows on branches of several fruit trees and parasitizes on them.
Look for the weed growing on branches of citrus-type fruit trees.
Such branches have fewer and smaller leaves than on healthy trees.
Fruits from affected branches are likely to drop early, and nothing will be harvested.
Monitor for branches attacked by the weed, especially during the rainy season.
Look for dead/ dried branches on the upper part of trees.
In severe cases, consider control action.

Chop and bury into soil at least 50cm depth.
Remove parasitic plants (with a pruning saw or secateurs) from larger heavily infected fruit tree branches and seal the cut surface with moist clay to prevent weed re-growth.

Restrictions: Synthetic herbicides cannot be used to kill the parasitic weeds on the fruit trees, as they will also kill the trees.

When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, PHI, max. number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources

Mixture or copper oxychloride based products (50% WP products at 1-2 g/L, check product label).
Spray on same day of pruning onto cut surfaces to prevent infection by pathogens.
Pre harvest interval 21 days; restricted re- entry interval 1-/2 day, copper oxychloride is toxic to soil and aquatic organisms
